marks_structure.extra_time_note: Yes — 15 minutes of reading time is given. Use it only to read the question paper and decide which OR options to attempt. Do not write anything.
marks_structure.internal_assessment_note: Passing the 80-mark theory paper is mandatory. Internal assessment (20 marks) is evaluated separately at school level.

paper_overview.sets_note: RBSE typically prints multiple sets. All sets contain the same questions, only the order differs. Write the set number on the cover page.
paper_overview.all_compulsory_note: Internal OR choice is available in Section C (Q13–Q16) and Section D (Q17–Q20).
paper_overview.ncert_enough: RBSE syllabus is based on NCERT (Aaroh Part 2, Vitan Part 2, Abhivyakti aur Madhyam). However, RBSE-specific reference books like SP Examination Idea are also essential.
paper_overview.official_scheme_note: Solve previous 5–7 years papers. Unseen passage topics, essay topics, and textbook questions repeat in similar formats.
paper_overview.reference_books_note: SP Examination Idea — Hindi Compulsory Class 12 (Science Publications, Jaipur) — most popular RBSE-specific guide.

question_types_in_exam.summary: RBSE Class 12 Hindi paper has 6 types of questions — MCQ (1 mark), Fill blank (1 mark), Very Short (1 mark), Short (2 marks), Long (3 marks), Essay-type (4–5 marks).

types.how_to_attempt: Write only the correct option letter (A/B/C/D). No explanation needed. Questions from textbook chapters, grammar, Abhivyakti aur Madhyam, and unseen prose/poetry.
types.mostly_from: Aaroh prose + poetry, Vitan, Abhivyakti aur Madhyam, unseen passages, practical grammar

types.how_to_attempt: Write one precise word or phrase. Topics: Shabd-Shakti types (Abhidha, Lakshana, Vyanjana), names of Alankar (figures of speech), technical terminology.
types.mostly_from: Types of word-power, Alankar (Yamak, Anupras, Rupak), technical Hindi terms

types.how_to_attempt: Give a direct factual answer in 1–2 sentences. Questions about author/poet names, work titles, events, definitions.
types.mostly_from: Aaroh prose + poetry, Vitan, Abhivyakti aur Madhyam

types.how_to_attempt: 2 marks = 1 main point + 1 supporting detail. Numbered bullet points are acceptable.
types.mostly_from: Abhivyakti aur Madhyam (Q6–8), Aaroh poetry (Q9–10), Aaroh prose (Q11–12)

types.how_to_attempt: 3 marks = Introduction/context (1) + Main content with 2–3 points (1.5) + Conclusion (0.5). For poet/author introduction: birth–death + works + language style.
types.mostly_from: Aaroh prose (Q13), Aaroh poetry (Q14), Vitan (Q15), Poet/Author introduction (Q16)

types.how_to_attempt: (1) Context — Name of work + Author. (2) Occasion — What the context is. (3) Explanation — Line-by-line meaning. (4) Feature — Literary/linguistic. Marks: Context(1) + Explanation(2) + Feature(1).
types.mostly_from: Famous poetry extracts from Aaroh (Q17), Important prose extract from Aaroh or Vitan (Q18)

types.how_to_attempt: Must follow the prescribed format strictly. For government memorandum/notification, follow RBSE's specific format.
types.mostly_from: Government memorandum (Pulse Polio, vaccination campaigns), notification, advertisement/tender

types.how_to_attempt: Substantive essay = Introduction + Body (4–5 paragraphs) + Conclusion. Relevant examples and quotes increase marks.

paper_pattern.internal_choice_note: Internal OR choice is available in Section C (Q13–Q16) and Section D (Q17–Q20).

types: Abhidha — Direct/literal meaning of a word, e.g., 'Gaay' means cow
Lakshana — When the primary meaning creates an obstacle, secondary meaning is inferred
Vyanjana — When neither Abhidha nor Lakshana expresses the meaning, implied/suggestive meaning

Fill blank: In Yamak Alankar, words have ________ (Avritti/repetition)
types: Anupras — Repetition of the same consonant sound
Yamak — Same word used in different meanings
Rupak — Superimposition of metaphor on subject

writing_section_formats.note: Contextual Explanation formats (Q17/Q18), Poet/Author Introduction format (Q16), Format Writing templates (Q19), Essay (Q20).

formats.format_name: Format for Contextual Explanation of Poetry Extract (Q17)
formats.structure: Context: These lines are taken from the poem _____, composed by _____. | Occasion: In these lines, the poet has expressed his/her views on the subject of _____. | Explanation: (Line-by-line meaning in simple language — 3–4 sentences) | Feature: In this poem, _____ Alankar / image is used. The language is _____.

formats.format_name: Format for Contextual Explanation of Prose Extract (Q18)
formats.structure: Context: The following prose extract is taken from the work _____, composed by _____. | Occasion: In this extract, the author says this in the context of _____. | Explanation: (Meaning and discussion — in 4–5 sentences) | Feature: In this extract, the author's _____ language style / perspective is revealed.

Birth: _____ was born in _____ on _____. | Education: His/Her education was completed at _____. | Major Works: His/Her major works are — (2–3 work titles) | Language and Style: His/Her language is _____. Style is _____. | Distinction/Award: He/She was honoured with the _____ Award.

formats.format_name: Format for Government Memorandum / Format Writing (Q19)
formats.structure: From: Designation, Department, State Government | To: Designation, Department | Letter Number: ___/Department/Year | Date: ___ | Subject: Regarding ...... | Reference: Previous letter or directive | Sir/Madam, | Main Content: What is to be done, when, and how | Signature + Designation + Seal
formats.tip: Correct format = 2 marks + Content = 3 marks = 5 marks total

formats.structure: Introduction/Preamble: Introduction of topic + importance (2–3 sentences) | Body: 4–5 paragraphs — one main point each | Examples/Facts: Relevant examples, statistics, or quotations | Conclusion: Summary + personal viewpoint
formats.tip: Introduction + Body (substantive content) + Language + Conclusion = 5 marks

practical_paper.practical_exam_note: RBSE Hindi has no practical. 80 theory + 20 IA = 100.

most_scoring_sections: Easy — MCQs from unseen passages, Shabd-Shakti fill blanks, very short factual answers. 35+ marks can be scored easily.
Easy to Medium — Abhivyakti aur Madhyam 6 marks (definition-based), Aaroh 8 marks (requires textbook knowledge).
most_difficult_sections: Medium to Hard — Contextual explanation format if not memorised will cost marks. Format writing format must be exactly correct.

tips: Q1's 18 MCQs — attempt all (no negative marking) — easy 15–16 marks
In Q3/Q4 unseen passages — take answers only from the passage — do not add personal knowledge
In Q2 fill blanks — write the Shabd-Shakti name clearly — 'Lakshana', 'Vyanjana', 'Abhidha'
In poet/author introduction — follow the format — birth, works, language style — missing any point will cost marks
In contextual explanation (Q17/Q18) — write Context first — work name + author name — earns 1 mark guaranteed
In format writing — keep 'Preshak', 'Prapt-karta', 'Vishay', 'Mahoday/Mahodaya' format absolutely correct
Essay word limit is 300 words — writing too much can also be penalised
Remember author/poet names of Aaroh chapters — used in both MCQ and very short answers
In internal choice (OR) questions — write only ONE option — do not write both
In Q5 very short — clearly write the question number of each answer

time_allocation.note: Read unseen passages (Q3/Q4). Decide which OR options to attempt in Q13–Q20. Decide which explanation (Q17/Q18) to write.
Q1 MCQ (20 min) + Q2 Fill blanks (8 min) + Q3/Q4 Unseen passages (12 min) + Q5 Very Short (10 min). No negative marking — attempt all.
Q6–Q12 — 7 short answers × approximately 3–4 min each. Write direct answer in 40 words.
Q13–Q16 — 4 long answers × approximately 6 min each. 60–80 words. Use numbered bullet points.
Q17/Q18 explanation × 10 min each + Q19 format 10 min + Q20 essay 10 min.
Check question numbers are correctly written? Did you accidentally write both OR options? Check essay word count.

targets.strategy: Section A MCQ (Q1) = 12–14 marks, Fill blanks (Q2) = 4–5 marks, Unseen passages (Q3+Q4) = 8–10 marks. Total = 24–29 marks.
focus_areas: Q1 — 18 MCQs (no negative marking — attempt all)
Q2 — Remember 3 types of Shabd-Shakti + 2–3 Alankar names
Q3 + Q4 — Unseen prose/poetry passages — read carefully and choose from options
Q5 — Very Short (direct facts from text — names, works, events)
chapters_to_skip_safely: Format writing (Q19) — if format is not known at all

targets.strategy: Full Section A (35–38) + 4–5 questions from Section B (8–10) = 43–48 marks. 1–2 Section C answers (3–6) as bonus.
focus_areas: Abhivyakti aur Madhyam — Q6/7/8 easy 6 marks
Shirish ke Phool, Bhaktin, Bazar Darshan — short answers
Aaroh poetry — Patang, Kavita ke Bahane — 2 marks each
Q16 — Poet/Author introduction format — easy 3 marks

targets.strategy: Full Section A (38–40) + Full Section B (14) + 3–4 Section C answers (9–12) + 2–3 Section D answers (9–13) = 70–79 marks.
focus_areas: All Aaroh prose chapters — Bhaktin, Bazar Darshan, Shirish, Pahalwaan ki Dholak
All Aaroh poetry — Tulsidas, Bachchan, Firaq, Alok Dhanwa
Vitan — Silver Wedding, Joojh, Ateet mein Dabe Paon
Memorise government memorandum and notification formats

targets.strategy: Maximum marks in all sections. Getting 18 marks in Section D alone makes 70+ possible.

internal_assessment.note: 20 marks internal assessment — school-level (projects, periodic tests, class participation).

exam_day_rules.extra_time_note: 15 minutes of reading time is given. Only read the question paper during this time — writing is prohibited.

answer_sheet_rules: Question number compulsory before each answer
Set number compulsory on cover page
Sequence not compulsory — attempt any order
Do not accidentally write both OR options — only one
Rough work on last page clearly labelled

pen_rules.note: Blue pen for main answers. Black for underlining.

exam_writing_rules.rough_work_rules: Rough work on last page — clearly label "रफ़ कार्य / ROUGH WORK".
